_doc.what: Tickers added to the CANDIDATE pool by hand, alongside the ETF-holdings, S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 sources.
_doc.why: A legitimate large-cap that no index source carries. The three index sources are not a census: a name can be well past any size or liquidity bar the system applies and still appear in none of them. Until it does the system cannot see it at all — not to reject it, to SEE it. This list is how such a name becomes visible.
_doc.why_not_only_new_listings: New listings are the most obvious instance of that rule, not the definition of it. A company that lists today joins no index for months. But a seasoned name can be equally invisible: outside the S&P 500, outside the Nasdaq-100, and below the ~10-deep top-holdings slice the ETF feed returns. ARWR — public since 2004, $12.5B, 251 bars — is that case. Scoping this list to new listings would leave the larger population unreachable for no principled reason.
_doc.what_it_does_not_do: It does not admit anything. An included name enters the candidate set and is then subject to every gate unchanged: composite score, price history, average volume, market cap, group membership, group rank. Nothing is waived. Inclusion buys consideration, never selection.
_doc.insufficient_history_is_correct: A newly listed name will not clear the history gate for months. Until it does it produces no ranking row and no error. That is the designed outcome, not a failure to fix — the gate is doing exactly what it exists to do, and the name becomes rankable on its own schedule.
_doc.precedence: EXCLUSION WINS. A ticker on both this list and universe.source.manual_exclusions is EXCLUDED. Exclusions are applied to the union of every source, last, so there is no ordering by which an inclusion can override one. To re-admit an excluded name, remove it from manual_exclusions — adding it here will not do it.
_doc.how_to_add: One object per ticker: `ticker`, `reason` (one line, why this name and why now), `added` (ISO date). Keep it short and keep it honest; the reason is what a future reader has to judge the entry by.
_doc.review: Entries are not self-retiring. When an index picks the name up it arrives from that source too and the entry here becomes redundant — harmless, but worth pruning at reconstitution.
